arm.title: Weapons
arm.hint: Every missile, bomb, rocket and torpedo in the game: stats from the game files, what each one is best at, comparison and the vehicles that carry it.
arm.noData: Weapon data isn't built yet: update the game data (Settings → Update game data).
arm.guideHint: Rankings are computed from the game files' stats only. Real performance also depends on the launch platform (radar, speed, altitude) and on game patches.
arm.fh.ccm: Counter-countermeasures: the seeker can reject flares
arm.fh.act: Own radar: no need to keep the target locked after launch
arm.fh.ins: Inertial guidance: flies toward the predicted target position before its seeker locks
arm.fh.dl: Datalink: the launcher's radar updates the missile in flight
arm.fh.loft: Climbs after launch to fly higher and further
arm.fh.ff: No need to guide or designate after launch
arm.fh.wire: Wire-guided: limited by wire length, unaffected by jamming
arm.col.name: Weapon
arm.colh.v: Speed the motor adds to the launch speed, from thrust, burn time and mass (no drag). Mach for missiles, m/s for rockets and ATGMs (cruise speed), knots for torpedoes
arm.colh.gl: Maximum load factor: how hard the missile can turn
arm.colh.ob: Off-boresight: how far off your nose the seeker can lock a target
arm.colh.trk: Seeker tracking rate: how fast a crossing target it can follow
arm.colh.lk: IR lock range on a target's engine exhaust (rear aspect)
arm.colh.aa: IR lock range from the front / side (all-aspect). Empty = rear-aspect only
arm.colh.tnt: Explosive mass × the explosive's strength, in kg of TNT: what matters for blast damage
arm.colh.br: Lowest battle rating (RB) of the vehicles that carry it
arm.colh.nv: Number of vehicles that carry it
arm.useh.dogfight: Max G, lock angle, seeker tracking rate, IRCCM, all-aspect lock
arm.useh.aspect: All-aspect lock range first, then speed, range and G
arm.useh.flares: IRCCM first, then tracking rate and G
arm.useh.bvr: Range, speed, active seeker, datalink, loft
arm.useh.ff: Needs no guidance after launch, then seeker range and agility
arm.useh.close: Max G, lock angle and acceleration off the rail
arm.useh.agile: Max G, speed and proximity fuse radius
arm.useh.tank: Penetration first, then speed and explosive
arm.useh.eff: TNT equivalent divided by the weapon's mass
arm.guide.aam_ir:
Dogfight: high G, a wide lock angle (off-boresight, best with a helmet sight) and a fast-tracking seeker win turning fights.
All-aspect missiles can lock a target from the front; rear-aspect ones only see the engine exhaust: fire behind the target.
IRCCM rejects flares: very valuable against modern aircraft that flare constantly.
The engine burn time and top speed decide how far the missile really reaches; range in the files is a best case.
Launch close and behind a non-maneuvering target for the best hit chance, and keep the target away from the sun.
arm.guide.aam_radar:
Semi-active (SARH) missiles need your radar to keep the lock until impact: you keep flying toward the enemy.
Active (ARH) missiles turn on their own radar near the target: fire, turn away, engage the next one.
Inertial guidance + datalink let you launch from long range; lofting climbs high and keeps energy for the end.
Radar missiles can be defeated by chaff and by the target flying perpendicular to you (notching): launch on targets flying toward or away from you.
For close range, prefer high-G missiles or an IR missile.
arm.guide.sam:
Fast missiles with high G reach maneuvering aircraft and helicopters before they can react.
SACLOS missiles need you to keep the crosshair (or radar track) on the target until impact; IR and active ones are fire & forget.
A large proximity fuse radius helps against small, agile targets like helicopters and drones.
Range decides how far you can hit attackers before they release their weapons.
arm.guide.atgm:
Penetration decides what you can kill from the front; tandem warheads defeat explosive reactive armor (ERA).
SACLOS / beam riders need you to keep aiming until impact: you stay exposed. Fire & forget (IR / TV / radar) lets you hide right after launch.
Fast missiles leave less time for the target to hide or shoot back; slow ones can be shot down by active protection systems.
On helicopters, long range lets you stay out of reach of SPAA.
arm.guide.agm:
TV / IR seekers are fire & forget: lock, launch, and you're free to leave. Laser needs the target designated until impact.
Anti-radiation missiles home on radars (SPAA and ships); radar-guided anti-ship missiles are made for ships.
Heavier warheads (TNT equivalent) kill tanks and destroy bases without a direct hit; penetration matters for small missiles on armored targets.
Long range lets you stay out of reach of air defenses.
arm.guide.gbomb:
Laser-guided bombs need the target designated (pod or another aircraft) until impact; GPS / INS and TV / IR ones are fire & forget.
Release high and fast to glide further: the further the target, the more energy you need.
TNT equivalent decides how close the impact must be to kill a tank or destroy a base.
arm.guide.bomb:
TNT equivalent is what kills: a near miss with a big bomb destroys a tank, a small one needs a direct hit.
Bases and airfields need a total TNT amount: big bombs reach it in fewer drops.
High-drag (retarded) bombs let you drop low and fast without being caught in the blast.
Heavier loads slow your aircraft: pick the lightest load that does the job.
arm.guide.rocket:
Against tanks, penetration matters: HEAT rockets go through roofs and sides, and hit-to-kill AP rockets work on light armor.
HE rockets with a big warhead are good against light vehicles, AA and soft targets.
Fast rockets are easier to aim at range; fire in salvos for a better chance to hit.
arm.guide.torpedo:
Speed reduces the time a ship has to turn away; range lets you launch from a safe distance.
The TNT equivalent decides how many torpedoes a large ship needs.
Check the launch limits in game (maximum speed and altitude for aircraft).
arm.note.su_r_73: A dogfight favourite: turns very hard and locks far off your nose, best with a helmet sight. Its IRCCM narrows the seeker, so flares still work head-on or from behind. Weaker at range.
arm.note.us_aim9m_sidewinder: Often called the best flare rejection among older IR missiles: it pauses when it sees flares, then looks again, so the target must flare and turn. Without a helmet sight it can't take wide-angle shots.
arm.note.fr_r_550_magic_2: Grouped with the R-73 as a strong short-range missile: narrow seeker view and good off-boresight shots.
arm.note.us_aim9l_sidewinder: The benchmark early all-aspect missile, carried by a huge number of aircraft. No IRCCM: flares plus a turn defeat it.
arm.note.su_r_27er: Widely seen as the strongest semi-active missile: fast, high G, it often wins long-range duels even fired second. Like every SARH missile, it's lost if your radar drops the lock. Its flight model is due for a rework.
arm.note.us_aim7m_sparrow: The standard NATO semi-active missile. Reliable, but generally rated below the R-27ER. Recently given a new flight model.
arm.note.us_aim7f_sparrow: A long guidance time helps at high altitude and speed; otherwise plays like the AIM-7M.
arm.note.uk_skyflash_temp: Very fast but with a short motor burn: excellent up close, mediocre past about 10 km.
arm.note.il_aspide_1a: Fast semi-active missile; works best on targets above you, where the ground doesn't confuse the radar.
arm.note.us_aim_120a: Fast, short time of flight, good at every range; some players find it inconsistent at holding lock. Buffed in the September 2026 update (better turning at low speed, smaller warhead).
arm.note.us_aim_120b: Plays like the AIM-120A: a fast, fire & forget all-rounder. Buffed in the September 2026 update.
arm.note.fr_mica_em: Seen as the hardest active missile to notch and very deadly up close; it bleeds speed when maneuvering at long range. Reworked in September 2026 (single-stage motor, longer range).
arm.note.su_r_77: Soviet active-radar missile; most players find it plays about like the AIM-120A/B.
arm.note.su_r_77_1: Some players call it the best all-round active missile, close to the MICA on wide-angle shots.
arm.note.cn_pl12: China's long-range active missile; its autopilot was reworked in 2026.
arm.note.cn_pl12a: Heavier than the PL-12 with more thrust and a longer burn since an April 2026 update.
arm.note.jp_aam4: Japan's long-range active missile; tuned several times in 2026.
arm.note.us_aim_54c: Rebuilt in June 2026: thrust changes with altitude, very high top speed. Made for very long shots on big, non-maneuvering targets.
arm.note.152mm_zur_9m311: Fast missile backed by 30 mm guns on the Tunguska; its radar only covers the front, and players rate it below newer systems.
arm.note.160mm_sam_1c: IR missiles that pull enough G to catch maneuvering attack jets and are described as very hard to flare. Short reach.
arm.note.239mm_9m331: Strong radar-command SAM (Tor); opinions differ on how hard it is to dodge.
arm.note.152mm_mim146: ADATS: proximity fuse and good reach against helicopters, but only 8 missiles on a slow, big vehicle.
arm.note.165mm_vt_1: Very strong inside about 8 km, loses agility beyond that.
arm.note.us_iris_t_sl: Early complaints were about limited speed and range against stand-off missiles like the Kh-38; its seeker was changed in late 2025.
arm.note.us_starstreak: Given a new flight model and fully physical guidance in March 2026; it was considered weak before.
arm.note.130mm_starstreak_hvm: Given a new flight model and fully physical guidance in March 2026; it was considered weak before.
arm.note.70mm_fim_92e: Short-range IR missile that locks late (under about 2 km). Flares alone only throw it off briefly: the pilot must also turn away.
arm.note.su_9m127: Long reach and a proximity fuse, so it also hits helicopters and aircraft: flexible. Rated good but not the best; its penetration was reduced.
arm.note.us_hellfire_agm_114_k: Big warhead and good penetration, but laser-guided: you keep the target designated until impact. Slow enough for SPAA to shoot down.
arm.note.spike_er: Fire & forget: launch, hide, engage the next target. Slow, and players often complain it hits barrels or breeches instead of the roof.
arm.note.110mm_spike_lr2: Fire & forget top-attack missile; slow, and damage on top hits can be inconsistent.
arm.note.euro_atgw3: Fire & forget and faster than the Spike; the Tiger that carries it is considered weak overall.
arm.note.130mm_9m120: Much faster than slow fire & forget missiles, with less reach and damage.
arm.note.lmur: Very long reach; not fully fire & forget against moving targets. The Mi-28NM carrying it is rated among the best top-tier helicopters.
arm.note.152mm_9m133: The standard Soviet heavy ATGM for tanks and IFVs: high penetration and long range.
arm.note.127mm_tow_2b: Top-attack missile; players complain about inconsistent damage when it strikes from above.
arm.note.us_agm_65b: Locks before launch then guides itself: very accurate, one or two hits kill a heavy tank. TV seeker: daylight only.
arm.note.us_agm_65d: Infrared Maverick: fire & forget like the TV versions, and it also works at night.
arm.note.uk_brimstone_dm: In game it's laser-guided with terminal homing only; its real radar fire & forget mode isn't modeled.
arm.note.su_kh_38mt: The most debated weapon in ground battles: long reach, thermal seeker, fire & forget, often launched from beyond SPAA range. Tuned in September 2025, still controversial.
arm.note.su_kh_29t: Huge warhead that can kill several vehicles at once; TV seeker, fire & forget.
arm.note.su_kh_29l: Huge warhead like the Kh-29T, but laser-guided: the target must stay designated.
arm.note.fr_as30l: Laser-guided with good reach and damage; seen as the Maverick's main rival around its BR.
arm.note.us_agm_88c: Anti-radiation missile: homes on enemy radars (SPAA, ships).
arm.note.us_gbu_12_paveway_2: Cheap, reliable 500 lb laser-guided bomb; keep the laser on the target until it lands.
arm.note.us_gbu_10_paveway_2: 2000 lb laser-guided bomb: kills several tanks or hard targets at once.
arm.note.us_2000lb_gbu_24: 2000 lb laser-guided bomb with a longer glide; the EGBU-24 adds GPS.
arm.note.us_gbu_39: Small glide bomb carried in large numbers, long glide range; release is capped at Mach 1.1.
arm.note.su_kab_500kr: TV-guided, fire & forget after lock, daylight only. Players say it locks much closer in game than in reality, and its warhead is about half a FAB-500's.
arm.note.su_kab_1500l: Very large laser-guided bomb that kills tanks over a wide area.
arm.note.fr_250kg_aasm_250_hammer_gps: Long-reach, rocket-boosted precision bomb; release limited to Mach 1 since September 2026.
arm.note.il_spice_1000: Long-reach precision glide bomb on Israeli jets.
arm.note.su_fab500sh: 500 kg bombs are the workhorse for killing tanks: much more forgiving than 250 kg (about 12 m destruction radius measured by players).
arm.note.us_2000lb_mk_84_ldgp: Big blast radius: kills several tanks bunched together and does heavy base damage.
arm.note.de_sc1800b: Base killer: one destroys a standard base on its own, a double-health base needs two.
arm.note.su_fab5000: Huge bomb for bases and airfields, with a very wide armor-destroying radius.
arm.note.de_sc2500: Huge base and airfield killer with a wide armor-destroying radius.
arm.note.su_s_8ko_rocket: 80 mm HEAT: good penetration, little explosive. Needs precise hits on the roof or sides, around 6 rockets for an MBT.
arm.note.us_hydra_70_m247: HEAT with decent penetration and enough blast to knock out open-topped vehicles with near misses. Fire in bursts.
arm.note.sws_oerlikon_oe82: Among the best penetration of any unguided rocket; found on few aircraft.
arm.note.su_s_24b_rocket: Big HE rocket: imprecise, but its blast hurts light armor and groups of vehicles.
arm.note.us_zuni_wafar_mk32: Big HE rocket: imprecise, but its blast hurts light armor and groups of vehicles.
arm.note.su_rbs82: WWII rocket whose penetration now depends on its speed (September 2026).
arm.note.jp_type91mod2_torpedo: The most forgiving aircraft torpedo: can be dropped fast and relatively high.
arm.note.us_mk13_torpedo: Late Mk.13: easy to drop at fairly high speed and altitude. Early versions need a slow, low approach.
arm.notesHint: Summarized from the official forum, wiki and Steam discussions (October 2026); patches can make them outdated.
arm.colh.acc: Acceleration off the rail (first-stage thrust / launch mass): how fast it gets up to speed, key at close range
arm.fh.ccm_r: IRCCM: the seeker pauses when it sees flares, then looks again — flare and turn to beat it
arm.fh.ccm_g: IRCCM: narrow tracking gate that ignores flares off the target's axis — flares still work head-on or from behind
arm.fh.ccm_rg: IRCCM: flare rejection + narrow tracking gate — the hardest to flare
arm.colh.yld: Explosive energy in kilotons (kt) or megatons (Mt) of TNT
arm.colh.bh: The bomb detonates this high above the ground (air burst)
arm.useh.effn: Yield divided by the bomb's mass: the most power for the least weight
arm.nukeCustom: No aircraft carries it in game: mount it on any pylon in WTFTD (Loadout → non-standard weapons).
arm.guide.nuke:
Yield is the bomb's energy in kilotons of TNT: 30 kt is six times 5 kt, and the megaton bombs are in another league.
They burst in the air above the target: almost nothing survives within a wide radius, including allies.
Drop from high and fast, then turn away: the carrier aircraft can be caught in the blast.
In regular battles they're rare (a reward in high-rank ground battles); in WTFTD you can mount any of them on any pylon to test them.
arm.fh.iw: In battle, its explosion wins the match for your team: the nuclear killstreak reward of ground battles. The game files give it no yield.
